learner_operation: Inspect the displayed array, count rows and columns independently, and report rows × columns. Entries and labels do not determine dimensions.

fixed_features.feature: One rectangular array and ordered rows × columns answer
fixed_features.justification: Tutorial d68f01b8-8bc6-59a1-8d80-d284abbcdf6e defines dimensions this way.

fixed_features.feature: Five radio choices or two numeric blanks
fixed_features.justification: These are the complete response contracts in supplied source questions.

fixed_features.feature: Normal row and column counts independently range 2 through 6
fixed_features.justification: Conservative finite domain spanning observed source workloads; covers 25 ordered decisions. Vector tutorial permits a later extension, but no supplied target question requires a vector and omission alone does not establish inadequate practice.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Change either independently; equal counts in original blanks are incidental.
answer_roles.observed: All 25 ordered shapes work in each template; both blank templates produce nonsquare matrices.

answer_roles.role: Correct radio dimension pair and position
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Any of five distinct bank members can be correct; position and label should not reveal the key.
answer_roles.observed: Normal construction samples a bank then chooses its correct shape uniformly. All five answer positions occur in 30 radio samples. Fixed-seed explicit boundary fixtures have correlated shuffle positions; they are not the delivered sampling distribution.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Change names and entries without altering dimension answer.
answer_roles.observed: Controlled A-to-Z rename and first entry 1-to-0 preserve 2×3 in all three templates.

coverage.case: All declared shapes in all three templates
coverage.result: 75 independent explicit cases; 25 ordered dimensions per template; all answers and solutions match.
90 random cases; full finite batch 25 unique shapes after 54 repeated-shape rejections.
Five shapes 6×2, 3×3, 4×6, 2×2, 5×5; 5/5 survive; no sign-only repeat. Radio and where-blank subgroups contain one member each, so no repeated shortcut inferred from a singleton.

counterfactuals.change: Append row [7,8,9] to fixed 2×3 array; keep name, original entries, template and radio bank fixed.
counterfactuals.expected: Answer changes from 2×3 to 3×3; column count remains 3; old row answer must fail.
counterfactuals.observed: All three templates update prompt, solution and accepted response. Native grader rejects old row count and accepts new count; radio checks every bank member. Actual UI screenshots show the added row.
counterfactuals.justification: Row count is defining evidence under tutorial 2968.

counterfactuals.change: Rename A to Z and change first entry 1 to 0; preserve all row and column boundaries.
counterfactuals.expected: 2×3 remains correct and all equivalent entries retain grading outcomes.
counterfactuals.observed: All templates preserve dimension key, solution counts and native grader outcomes; rendered name/entry change is visible. Choice IDs and order can change because identities are content-derived.
counterfactuals.justification: Values and matrix name are not arguments of the dimensions rule.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Select first offered choice without counting
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Baseline 1/5: random choice among five radio options.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Count rows then repeat that number in the column blank
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Baseline 1/5: after counting rows, uniform guess among five permitted column counts. Only 5/30 successes; wording does not imply equal dimensions.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Count rows then repeat that number in the column blank
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Baseline 1/5: after counting rows, uniform guess among five permitted column counts. Only 5/30 successes; wording does not imply equal dimensions.

shortcut_probes.cue: Let wording in actual runner batch
shortcut_probes.strategy: Count rows then repeat as columns
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Only 1/3 correct; two nonsquare counterexamples survive delivery. Baseline is uniform column guess among five permitted counts, not a significance claim for three cases.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Count displayed rows and columns in order
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Shape is answer-bearing evidence by the lesson definition. Counting it is the intended operation; baseline 1/25 is a blind ordered-dimension guess.

stages_examined: learner history exclusion and easy-band selection rules
delivery.result: 90/90 independent and 5/5 runner records survive. Shape distributions unchanged. All generated records are easy, so positive easy-band weighting does not select a shape by template; histories remove seen records. Captured current bank has 12 easy and two unrated candidates; none is retired.

limitations: No finite probe rules out every incidental shortcut.
Source q-139628 replay is unsupported and fails separately; no decision-variation pass waives source fidelity.
Vectors are not generated; finite observed-workload domain is disclosed, not claimed as all possible matrix dimensions.
Live policy/history and concurrent inventory changes are not captured. See exact conditional selection analysis in delivery-selection-results.json.
